interest: A 1938 memo names Konoye and Hirota, not the military, as drivers of aggressive China policy.
overview: A 1936 cross-reference on opposition to Japan's seditious literature bill, and an April 1938 Far Eastern Affairs memo on the China Economic Affairs Bureau and Japanese policy in China.

people.name: Nobumasa Suetsugu
people.role: Admiral and Japanese Minister of Home Affairs

people.name: Katsuo Okazaki
people.role: Japanese Consul General at large in China

people.name: John M. Allison
people.role: U.S. Foreign Service Officer / Consul at Nanking

people.name: James K. Penfield
people.role: Officer, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, U.S. Department of State

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 1876 concerning public and parliamentary opposition to the seditious literature bill in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Tokyo Despatch No. 1876 (May 1936) on opposition to the seditious literature bill, passed only in amended form.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Tokyo Despatch No. 1876 on Freedom of Speech and the Seditious Literature Bill

subfiles.about: Memorandum summarizing Japanese government plans for the China Economic Affairs Bureau, leadership factionalism, and intelligence on Japan's military and economic limits in China.
subfiles.summary: James K. Penfield reviews Japan's new China Economic Affairs Bureau, Konoye's and Hirota's chauvinism, and Okazaki's disclosures of financial and military worries.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by James K. Penfield on Proposed China Economic Affairs Bureau and Japan's Plans for the Yangtze Region
